back: To walk unevenly because one leg hurts.
To walk awkwardly (e.g., shoes too tight or feet hurt).
To walk unsteadily (e.g., if drunk or ill).
To walk nearly falling on an uneven surface.
To make sudden or irregular movements (e.g., on a moving ship).
To walk quietly and on toes not to be heard.
To walk at an easy, gentle pace for pleasure.
To walk with long, purposeful steps.
To walk in a proud way, chest held out, to look important.
To walk with firm, heavy steps for a long time.
To walk pressing repeatedly with feet (often to destroy).
To push the foot down heavily (e.g., in anger).
To walk with heavy, slow steps when tired or with difficulty.
To run or move quickly to catch someone or something.
To walk or flow in a winding way (often of water or people).
